chunks: And it has been narrated from him (peace be upon him) this meaning in another wording,
which is his saying: The heart of the fool is in his mouth, and the tongue of the wise man is in his heart.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between a fool and a wise person according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi presents this aphorism as a concise definition of wisdom (hikmah) and folly, emphasizing that true intelligence is measured by self-restraint rather than eloquence. In Shia scholarly tradition, this reflects the concept of 'tadabbur' (deep reflection) preceding speech, aligning with the Prophet's description of the wise as those who are 'slow to speak and quick to listen.'

en.sayed-ali-raza: 41. This very sense has been related from Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, in a different version as follows:
The heart of a fool is in his mouth while the tongue of the wise man is in his heart.
